📜 12 MARCH 2020: BITCOIN LOST HALF IN A DAY On 12 March 2020, Bitcoin fell about 50% in a day. It was not a crypto event. A pandemic panic was crashing stocks, oil and gold at once, and crypto was the most sellable thing a lot of people held. The drop was violent because it was borrowed. Over $1B of longs were force-closed in 24h, each forced sale feeding the next. On MakerDAO, a jammed network let a bot win collateral for a $0 bid. At the lows, the top exchange went dark for 25 minutes and the cascade paused. The plumbing that broke got rebuilt. That is why circuit breakers are standard now. 📖 Free 12-chapter Playbook: blocknbull.xyz/playbook 🔗 Trading? Stay on FIU-registered exchanges. 📡 40,000 BITCOIN LEFT BINANCE AS PRICE FELL Bitcoin slid toward $84,000 this week in a macro shakeout. On the chain, the money moved the other way. About 40,000 BTC, near $3.3 billion, left Binance between 20 Sep and 5 Oct, its fastest withdrawal pace since June 2023. On 6 October alone roughly 14,300 coins left in net terms, the biggest single-day net outflow CryptoQuant has confirmed. Whales did the opposite with stablecoins, sending them onto the exchange as what analysts call dry powder. Heavy outflows usually mean coins moving to self-custody, which many read as accumulation. 🎓 BULL SCHOOL · WHERE YOUR CRYPTO IS KEPT An Indian exchange just lost $16 million from an old wallet. CoinDCX says users kept paying into deposit addresses it had retired, and it covered the loss itself. Every big exchange splits your crypto two ways. A hot wallet is online and pays out withdrawals fast. A cold wallet is offline, and most coins sit there. Hackers go after what is online. Offline is not perfect either: Bybit lost about $1.5 billion from a cold wallet in February 2025. Your rule: keep on an exchange only what you are trading. Never share your 12 recovery words with anyone, including "support". 🔗 Trading? Stay on FIU-registered exchanges.
